args.body:
## Job
Create a team document in the docs project (deliverables/, reports/, handbook/, minutes/) that satisfies both its content acceptance criteria and the mandatory document convention.

## When to use
A ticket asks for a file in deliverables/, reports/, handbook/ or minutes/ of the docs project and a pre-merge check enforces a document convention, even when agenium.toml [checks] pre_merge is empty.

## Steps
1. Read an existing reference document of the same repo (e.g. deliverables/hello.txt) to copy the exact convention instead of guessing; README.md names the document folders.
2. Confirm the owning team name and write the first line exactly `Owner: <team>` (one space after the colon, no trailing spaces, no other prefix).
3. Put the required ticket content on the following line(s); the Owner line does not replace or conflict with content criteria.
4. Write the file with the file tool (write_file/edit_file) so parent directories are created and the text is UTF-8 without a BOM; never use PowerShell `>` (UTF-16) or Out-File/Set-Content -Encoding utf8 (adds a BOM) on Windows.
5. Verify the raw leading bytes, not just the text: read the file back and check the first bytes are the ASCII of `Owner:` (first byte 0x4F, no EF BB BF), line endings are LF (0x0A) and no CR (0x0D) if the repo uses LF.
6. Re-check the acceptance criterion literally (e.g. regex -match 'standup') on the file as stored.

## Tools
- read_file / list_dir to find and copy the reference document convention.
- write_file (or edit_file) to create the document with LF endings and no BOM.
- shell with PowerShell for byte-level proof: `[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes(path)` printed as hex and a `-match` content check.

## Proof
Evidence must show (a) the stored file's first 16 bytes in hex equal `4F 77 6E 65 72 3A 20 64 6F 63 73 2D 74 65 61 6D` (i.e. `Owner: docs-team`, no BOM) followed by 0A, and (b) an explicit check that the required content is present in the file. Paste the hex dump and the content-match output in the report; a statement that the line "looks right" in an editor is not proof.

[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-2 {"project":"docs"}) In the docs project, documents such as deliverables/hello.txt and reports/weekly.txt are written with LF line endings and no BOM.

[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-2 {"project":"docs"}) In the docs project, deliverables/hello.txt is the reference example of the document convention: first line 'Owner: docs-team', second line the document content.

[Fact untrusted w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) A passing review approval does not guarantee merge: check README.md at the repo root before writing files to discover document conventions (such as where team documents live) that the ticket description may omit, and run through them before considering a deliverable ticket done.

[Lesson w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) When a first line must match exactly, verify the raw leading bytes (no BOM) before submitting, since a BOM makes an otherwise correct first line fail the exact-match pre-merge check.

[Lesson w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) When creating a document under deliverables/ or reports/ in the docs project, add the 'Owner: <team>' first line before submitting; this does not conflict with content acceptance criteria—the required content goes on the following line—because the pre-merge check rejects documents missing it even when acceptance criteria are met.

[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) In the docs project, agenium.toml has an empty [checks] pre_merge value, yet the Owner-first-line document rule is still enforced at merge time, so the convention must be read from the repo docs/spec rather than from that field.

[Fact untrusted w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) The docs project stores team documents in deliverables/, reports/, handbook/ and minutes/ (deliverables in deliverables/, reports in reports/), and keeps project configuration in agenium.toml at the repo root.

[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"product":"agenium"}) Agenium's pre-merge check validates project document rules (such as the Owner first line) in addition to the ticket's acceptance criteria, so work must satisfy both before merging.
[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) In the docs project, every team document placed in deliverables/ or reports/ must have its first line exactly 'Owner: docs-team' (its owning team).
